text:
omar: Heads-up: we just saw a KV/prefix cache hit-rate collapse on rtm-prod-6 after the prefix rekey rollout. p99 token-latency spiked ~2x. Not sure yet if it's noisy tenant or the rehash logic.

sam: Oncall pinged and looking now :eyes:. Which flag rolled? any recent kernel/batching changes?

omar: We enabled kv.rehash_on_rotate=true in the rotation job at 10:11 UTC and started rotating prefixes for tenant-42 to reduce collisions. No kernel changes in that deploy. Batching window and kernel-selection are unchanged in the service config.

claire: Can you paste the metrics snapshot?

omar: metrics dump (10:18 UTC):
```
kv_prefix_hitrate{shard=\"s12\"} 0.042
kv_prefix_hitrate{shard=\"s13\"} 0.008
cache_evictions_total{reason=\"rehash\"} 124012
cache_entries{shard=\"s12\"} 8421
serving_p99_latency_ms{model=\"gpt-small\"} 320
```

mike: wow that's brutal. Looks like rehash triggered mass remap and priming didn't happen, so eviction pressure spiked. Could also be the rehash algorithm touching many buckets concurrently -> locking/backpressure.

jordan: Agree. Also see batching backlog on the target nodes which can increase KV cache working set due to request ordering changes. If batcher holds more tokens while waiting, memory footprint goes up and triggers evictions.

omar: repro commands we ran: `curl http://rtm-prod-6/metrics | grep kv_prefix_hitrate -n` and `curl http://rtm-prod-6/diagnostics?shard=s12` returned the above. Devops-bot posted rotation job logs around 10:12 showing concurrent rehash on 20 worker threads.

devops-bot: rotation-job/tenant-42 started at 10:11:37, concurrent_workers=20, rehash_mode=full, batch_window_ms=5

sam: Immediate mitigation options?

omar: We first toggled kv.rehash_on_rotate=false at 10:25 to stop further rotates. Then increased kv.cache_target_size by 20% for the affected shard pool to buy time. Also primed the top-200 prefixes manually using a small generator job.

claire: commands used to prime (run from ops jump host):
```
for p in $(cat top_prefixes.txt); do
  curl -s -XPOST \"http://rtm-prod-6/gen?prefix=$p\" >/dev/null &
done
```

mike: After rollback + priming, hit-rate climbed back. Snapshot 10:40 UTC:
```
kv_prefix_hitrate{shard=\"s12\"} 0.81
kv_prefix_hitrate{shard=\"s13\"} 0.79
cache_evictions_total{reason=\"rehash\"} 124200
serving_p99_latency_ms{model=\"gpt-small\"} 120
```

jordan: Root cause hypothesis: full concurrent rehash overwhelmed cache priming process and changed hot-key locality. Combined with batcher backlog momentarily increasing each request's working set, we hit eviction storm. The rehash algorithm is O(n) touching many buckets; doing that concurrently on many workers causes large transient churn.

sam: Action items: 1) add a canary gate for rehash_on_rotate with staged worker concurrency (1 -> 2 -> 5) and throttled rehashing, 2) add preflight metric to simulate priming cost and estimate working set delta, 3) make kernel selection aware of short-term memory headroom to prefer memory-light kernels when eviction risk high, 4) update runbook for manual prime and cache-size bump.

omar: +1 on all. I'll file the follow-up ticket with traces and the rotation job logs attached. Also we should audit other tenants where rotation ran last 24h.

claire: Also propose adding a telemetry alarm: if evictions spike > 5k/min during a rotation, auto-throttle the rotation job.

mike: note: regression possibility — if a recent kernel micro-optim changed allocation burst patterns, it could amplify the eviction. We'll profile kernel allocation hotspots during a controlled rehash in staging.

devops-bot: rotation-job/tenant-42 status: rolled back at 10:25:12 by sam, priming jobs started at 10:28:05, cache_size increased on shard-pool s12 at 10:30:10.

sam: postmortem plan: short incident blameless writeup, timeline, metrics, and proposed mitigations. tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml (kernel), and eng-oncall.

omar: TL;DR: rehash_on_rotate + concurrent_workers=20 triggered eviction storm -> p99 spike; rollback + priming + cache bump recovered hit-rate to ~0.8. Need throttled rehash + preflight priming + memory-aware kernel heuristics.
